observations: Photo 0: a greasy engine assembly with gearbox attached, sitting on wooden pallets outdoors, heavy wiring and hoses visible, no readable tag or part number.
Photo 1: same unit from another angle, still cluttered with engine wiring, visible rust and dirt coating the transmission housing, no legible markings.
Photo 2: the bare gearbox/transmission tail-end on the ground next to a person's foot, caked in mud/debris, no plate, sticker or stamped number visible.
Watermark reads 'GEARUP INC.' on all photos, suggesting a parts-yard stock photo rather than a photo of the actual unit for sale.
No VIN, part number, or Ford casting marks are visible in any photo.

identity.kind: engine/transmission (gearbox) assembly, claimed for Ford Econoline E150/E250/E350 V8

claims.claim: Gearbox for Ford Econoline E150/E250/E350 V8
claims.evidence: No Ford casting marks, tags, or part numbers visible in photos 0-2 to confirm fitment.
No shift pattern, bell-housing bolt pattern, or stamped ID visible.
No import sticker, customs tag, or dealer paperwork shown.
No shipping label, container tag, or documentation visible.
No video of the unit running or being bench-tested; photos show a static, dirty unit.
No odometer, service sticker, or paperwork shown; heavy external grime visible in all photos.
Bolts/case seams are caked in dirt in photo 1, making tamper-evidence impossible to judge from the image.

risks.risk: Internal transmission wear or damage (clutch packs, gears, seals) cannot be assessed from external photos.
risks.proof: A video of the gearbox being turned/tested on a stand, or a bench-test clip showing shifting through gears.
risks.if_unproven: priced as not working / worst-case condition

risks.risk: Exact model/fitment (E150 vs E250 vs E350, 2WD vs 4WD, engine displacement) cannot be confirmed without a casting number or tag.
risks.proof: Close-up photo of the stamped casting number or ID tag on the transmission case.
risks.if_unproven: priced as generic unverified fitment, not premium exact-match

risks.risk: Mileage and true origin (Belgium/tokunbo) unverifiable; heavy dirt and grime suggest yard storage, not recent low-mileage use.
risks.proof: Import/customs paperwork or dealer invoice with mileage and origin stamp.

risks.risk: Listing photos carry a third-party watermark (GEARUP INC.), raising doubt the photos are of the actual unit being sold.
risks.proof: Fresh, unwatermarked photos taken by the seller today, ideally with a timestamp or newspaper.
risks.if_unproven: treated as unverified stock photo, discounting seller credibility

proof_requests: Close-up of the casting/part number stamped on the transmission case.
Video of the gearbox being tested (turning input shaft, shifting gears, no play/knock).
Fresh photos without the GEARUP INC. watermark, taken at the seller's current location.
Any import/customs documentation showing Belgium origin and mileage.
response.reason: The item is clearly an engine/transmission assembly of a type (American V8 gearbox) but none of the seller's condition or origin claims can be verified from the photos, so it must be priced at worst-case condition against comparable unverified US-drive V8 gearbox listings.
